body_markdown:
**Discover the best YouTube channels to learn English in 2026. Improve pronunciation, vocabulary, fluency, and confidence with practical tips and MySivi.**


Have you ever watched an entire **[English podcast](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/learn-english-naturally-in-2026-7-podcasts-that-build-real-fluency/)**


, understood every third word, and still replied to your friend with “Yes, bro, same”? Congratulations. You have officially entered the


*I-can-understand-English-but-can’t-speak-it* club.


The good news? You don’t need to move to London, hire a private tutor, or suddenly become the main character in an American sitcom to improve your English.


Sometimes, the best classroom is already sitting in your pocket:


[YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/)


.


The platform offers thousands of free videos covering **[English pronunciation](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/fix-s-vs-sh-pronunciation-speak-clearly-in-english-mysivi/)**


, grammar, **[vocabulary](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/top-50-elevated-english-words-that-sharpen-daily-speech/)**


, everyday conversations, accents, storytelling, psychology, and personal development. Whether you’re a student preparing for **[interviews](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/practice-for-a-job-interview-english-speaking-skills-that-get-you-hired/)**


, a professional trying to sound more confident in meetings, or someone who wants to stop translating every sentence in their head, there’s a channel for you.


But here’s the catch:


**watching English content and speaking English confidently are two different skills.** You can binge-watch 50 videos about pronunciation and still panic when someone asks, “Could you introduce yourself?”


That’s why this guide goes beyond a typical list of English teachers. We’ve grouped some of the best YouTube channels to learn English by learning goals, from mastering pronunciation and understanding native speakers to building better habits, expanding your worldview, and practising real conversations.


You’ll also discover how to turn your favourite videos into an everyday English-speaking routine using a simple method:


**Watch, Shadow, Speak.**


Let’s find your next favourite channel.


## Quick Answer: Which YouTube Channels Are Best for Learning English?


The best YouTube channel depends on what you want to improve. Here are some useful starting points:

**[Speak English With Vanessa](https://www.youtube.com/@SpeakEnglishWithVanessa)**

Learning mindset and motivation


**[Canguro English](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Canguro+English+official)**

**[Rachel’s English](https://www.youtube.com/@rachelsenglish)**


**Our recommendation:** Choose two or three channels that complement each other. For example, practice English speaking using MySivi, learn pronunciation from Rachel’s English, build listening skills with BBC Learning English, and then practice speaking using the expressions you’ve learned.


You don’t need 20 subscriptions. You need a learning routine you can actually stick to.


## Best YouTube Channels for English Pronunciation, Vocabulary and Fluency


If your goal is to speak English more clearly, understand native speakers, and express yourself naturally, start with channels that teach the language in context.


### **1. Rachel’s English — Master American English Pronunciation**


**Best for:** **[Pronunciation](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/fix-s-vs-sh-pronunciation-speak-clearly-in-english-mysivi/)** , connected speech, accent awareness, and speaking clarity.


**Recommended level:** Beginner to advanced, depending on the lesson.


**[Watch Rachel’s English on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@rachelsenglish)**


Ever wondered why native English speakers seem to swallow half their words and still expect everyone to understand them?


Welcome to connected speech.


Rachel’s English breaks down American English pronunciation into manageable lessons. You’ll find explanations of mouth position, vowel and consonant sounds, word stress, rhythm, intonation, and the way words blend during everyday conversations.


Instead of simply memorising how a word is spelt, you can observe how it’s pronounced and practice producing the sound yourself.


**Try this:** Pick a short pronunciation lesson. Listen to one sentence, pause the video, and repeat it three times. Pay attention to the stress and rhythm rather than copying individual sounds alone.


**Gen Z example:** Your textbook might teach you every letter in a sentence. Real-life English might connect those words so smoothly that your brain goes, “Wait, did they say one word or seven?”


Rachel’s lessons can help you understand what’s happening.


### **2. English with Lucy — Sound More Natural in British English**


**Best for:** British pronunciation, vocabulary, idioms, grammar, and polished communication.


**Recommended level:** Beginner to advanced, depending on the topic.


**[Watch English with Lucy on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@EnglishwithLucy)**


Want to understand British expressions without feeling as though you’ve accidentally walked into a period drama?


English with Lucy makes British English approachable through structured lessons covering **[vocabulary](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/top-50-elevated-english-words-that-sharpen-daily-speech/)**


, pronunciation, common mistakes, **[grammar](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/do-you-need-perfect-grammar-to-speak-fluent-english/)**


, and natural expressions.


Her content is especially useful for learners who want to expand their vocabulary and understand the differences between textbook English and the way people communicate in everyday situations.


For example, knowing the word “tired” is useful. Learning expressions such as “I’m exhausted,” “I’m worn out,” and “I’m knackered” helps you recognize different levels of emphasis and informal British usage.


**Try this:** Write down three new expressions from a lesson and create a sentence about your own life using each one.


The goal isn’t to use fancy vocabulary in every sentence. It’s to have more ways to express the same idea.


### **3. Learnex — English Lessons Through Hindi**


**Best for:** Hindi-speaking beginners who want clear explanations of English concepts.


**Recommended level:** Beginner to intermediate.


**[Find Learnex on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Learnex+English+lessons+through+Hindi+official)**


Sometimes, the problem isn’t that **[English grammar](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/do-you-need-perfect-grammar-to-speak-fluent-english/)** is impossible. It’s that the explanation is more confusing than the grammar itself.


Learnex offers English lessons through Hindi, helping learners understand grammar rules, **[vocabulary](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/top-50-elevated-english-words-that-sharpen-daily-speech/)**


, common errors, and everyday English expressions.


For learners in India who are more comfortable understanding a concept in Hindi before applying it in English, this bilingual approach can make the learning process less intimidating.


For instance, instead of memorising a tense formula without understanding it, learn when to use the tense and practise creating sentences about your daily routine.


**Try this:** Learn one grammar rule, write five original sentences, and read them aloud without translating each word separately.


**A gentle reminder:** Hindi can be a useful starting point, but gradually try forming simple thoughts directly in English. Your brain doesn’t need to hold a translation meeting before every sentence.


### **4. BBC Learning English — Build a Consistent Learning Habit**


**Best for:** Listening, grammar, **[vocabulary](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/top-50-elevated-english-words-that-sharpen-daily-speech/)**


, news-related English, and short daily lessons.


**Recommended level:** Beginner to advanced, depending on the series.


**[Watch BBC Learning English on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@bbclearningenglish)**


If you struggle to find time for English practice between college, work, commuting, and scrolling through reels, BBC Learning English is worth exploring.


Its educational content includes short lessons, vocabulary explanations, pronunciation guidance, and discussions of current topics. Series such as


*6 Minute English* offer a convenient way to practise listening in manageable sessions.


You can also learn expressions used in news reporting, professional communication, and everyday conversation.


**Try this:** Watch one short video during breakfast. Write down two useful expressions and summarize the topic aloud in three sentences.


You don’t need to turn every morning into an **[IELTS](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/score-high-in-ielts-toefl-using-english-speaking-apps/)**


examination. Six focused minutes can be a practical starting point.


### **5. Speak English With Vanessa — Practise Natural Everyday English**


**Best for:** Conversational English, listening, common expressions, and speaking confidence.


**Recommended level:** Beginner to intermediate, with lessons suitable for different abilities.


**[Watch Speak English With Vanessa on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@SpeakEnglishWithVanessa)**


You may know the grammar rules perfectly and still struggle when someone asks, “So, what did you do over the weekend?”


This is where conversational English becomes important.


Vanessa’s channel focuses on practical expressions, everyday conversations, listening, and the natural patterns people use when speaking English. Her friendly teaching style makes it useful for learners who want to move beyond memorized textbook dialogues.


For example, instead of replying “I am fine” to every greeting, you can practice expressions such as:


- “I’m doing pretty well, thanks!”


- “It’s been a busy week.”


- “Can’t complain!”


- “I’m hanging in there.”


**Try this:** Pause after a model sentence and answer the same question using your own information. Don’t just repeat the example—make it yours.


### **6. Learn English with Bob the Canadian — Learn Vocabulary from Everyday Life**


**Best for:** Practical vocabulary, everyday situations, and understanding English in context.


**Recommended level:** Beginner to intermediate.


**[Find Bob the Canadian on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Learn+English+with+Bob+the+Canadian+official)**


You don’t learn a language only by studying definitions. You learn it by connecting words with situations.


Bob the Canadian teaches English through familiar subjects and real-world contexts, making his videos useful for learners who want to understand the **[vocabulary](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/top-50-elevated-english-words-that-sharpen-daily-speech/)**


used in daily life.


Think shopping, travel, work, household objects, and ordinary interactions. These are precisely the situations where knowing the right expression can make communication easier.


For example, learning “Could you give me a moment?” is useful when you need time to think during a conversation.


**Try this:** Pick five objects around you and describe each one in English. Then explain what you did today without writing a script first.


It’s simple, practical, and surprisingly effective as a speaking exercise.


### **7. EnglishClass101 — Explore English Lessons for Different Levels**


**Best for:** Topic-based learning, vocabulary, grammar, listening, and structured lesson exploration.


**Recommended level:** Beginner to advanced, depending on the video.


**[Watch EnglishClass101 on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=EnglishClass101+official+YouTube)**


Some days, you need help with pronunciation. Other days, you need to understand a common phrase or practise a particular conversation.


EnglishClass101 provides a broad collection of English-learning videos that you can explore according to your interests and current level.


This variety is helpful when you want to build a personal study routine rather than follow only one type of lesson.


**Try this:** Choose one specific topic, such as introducing yourself, ordering food, or preparing for a job interview. Learn the expressions, then create a short dialogue using them.


Avoid opening ten unrelated lessons in one sitting. Your watch history might look productive, but your brain deserves a syllabus.


### **8. Learn English with TV Series — Learn from Movies and Shows**


**Best for:** Listening comprehension, idioms, informal English, and understanding natural speech.


**Recommended level:** Intermediate to advanced, with some accessible lessons for beginners.


**[Watch Learn English with TV Series on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@LearnEnglishWithTVSeries)**


What if your next English lesson felt more like watching your favourite show than sitting through a grammar lecture?


Learn English with TV Series breaks down scenes from popular entertainment, helping learners understand expressions, pronunciation, vocabulary, humour, and cultural references.


This can be especially useful because real conversations often sound different from carefully prepared classroom dialogues. People speak quickly, connect words, use **[idioms](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/speak-smart-50-everyday-english-idioms-with-hindi-meaning/)**


, and occasionally mumble.


**Try this:** Select a short scene. Watch it once for the overall meaning, then replay it with subtitles. Write down three expressions and imitate one complete line.


For example, if a character says, “You have got to be kidding me,” practise the entire expression instead of memorizing only the word “kidding.”


**Gen Z translation:** Your favourite sitcom can become an English lesson. Just don’t claim you’re studying English when you’ve watched six episodes and learned only the word “literally.”


### **9. Pronunciation with Emma — Improve Your British English Clarity**


**Best for:** British pronunciation, grammar explanations, and targeted language difficulties.


**Recommended level:** Beginner to advanced, depending on the lesson.


**[Find Emma’s lessons on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Pronunciation+with+Emma+engVid+official)**


If you frequently confuse similar-sounding words or struggle with particular pronunciation patterns, focused lessons can be more useful than general English videos.


Emma’s lessons through engVid cover practical English topics, including pronunciation and grammar. Look for the specific lesson that matches your difficulty rather than watching videos randomly.


For example, compare words such as “ship” and “sheep.” The difference between their vowel sounds can change the meaning completely.


**Try this:** Listen to the target sound, repeat it slowly, and then practice it inside a complete sentence. Record yourself and compare your pronunciation with the model.


Remember, the aim is clear communication—not trying to erase your identity or imitate an accent perfectly.


### **10. English with Yuliya — Practice English Shadowing**


**Best for:** Learners seeking focused listening, pronunciation, and fluency exercises.


**Recommended level:** Intermediate learners and above, depending on the lesson.


**[Find English with Yuliya on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=English+with+Yuliya+shadowing+official)**


Shadowing is a language-learning technique in which you listen to a speaker and repeat their words almost simultaneously, paying attention to rhythm, stress, and intonation.


English with Yuliya is worth exploring if you want to incorporate this style of practice into your routine. Review individual videos to find exercises and materials that suit your current level.


**Try this:** Choose a 20–30-second clip. Listen once, replay it while speaking along, and repeat the exercise several times.


Don’t worry if you sound awkward at first. Your first attempt at shadowing might sound like your brain and your mouth are working different shifts. That’s normal.


## Best YouTube Channels for Learning English Through Mindset and Motivation


Improving your English isn’t only about learning new words. It also involves understanding how you learn, managing frustration, and staying consistent when progress feels slow.


These channels can help you explore those ideas while giving you more English listening practice.


### **11. Canguro English — Understand How Language Learning Works**


**Best for:** Language-learning strategies, motivation, and overcoming learning plateaus.


**Recommended level:** Intermediate and above, depending on the topic.


**[Watch Canguro English on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Canguro+English+official+YouTube)**


Have you ever studied English consistently for weeks and then felt as if nothing had changed?


Language learning can feel frustrating when you measure progress only by how fluent you sound today.


Canguro English explores the learning process, including motivation, learning strategies, vocabulary acquisition, and the mindset behind language development. Its content encourages learners to think critically about how they study rather than automatically collecting more grammar rules.


**Try this:** After watching a video, explain its main argument aloud in English. This way, you’re learning about learning while practising your communication skills.


The important lesson is to build a repeatable system rather than constantly search for a magical shortcut.


### **12. English with Ulle — Make Practice More Interactive**


**Best for:** Learners who enjoy a mix of vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, humour, and quizzes.


**Recommended level:** Check individual lessons to find the right starting point.


**[Find English with Ulle on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=English+with+Ulle+official+YouTube)**


Some people learn best through structured explanations. Others prefer quizzes, humour, and activities that make them participate.


English with Ulle combines different English-learning formats, offering an option for learners who want variety in their practice.


**Try this:** Before revealing a quiz answer, say your answer aloud and explain why you chose it. This transforms a passive quiz into an opportunity to practise speaking.


After all, watching someone else answer questions is not quite the same as answering them yourself.


## Best YouTube Channels for Lifestyle, Productivity and Personal Growth


Want to improve your English while learning about habits, confidence, relationships, or intentional living?


Lifestyle content can provide a refreshing alternative to traditional English lessons. It also exposes you to the language people use when discussing real experiences and personal opinions.


### **13. Simple Happy Zen — Learn Through Calm, Thoughtful Content**


**Best for:** Minimalism, intentional living, reflection, and relaxed listening practice.


**Recommended level:** Intermediate learners and above, depending on the video.


**[Find Simple Happy Zen on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Simple+Happy+Zen+Vera+official)**


Not every English-learning session needs to feel like an exam.


Simple Happy Zen explores minimalism, intentional living, and ways to create a calmer, more meaningful lifestyle. Its reflective style can provide an opportunity to listen to thoughtful explanations and encounter vocabulary related to habits, priorities, and well-being.


**Try this:** Watch a short video and summarise its central idea in your own words. Then share one opinion about the topic.


For example: “I think reducing distractions helps me concentrate better when I’m studying.”


That single sentence practises vocabulary, sentence structure, and expressing an opinion.


### **14. Lana Blakely — Explore Confidence, Relationships and Life Questions**


**Best for:** Conversational listening, self-reflection, confidence, and personal growth.


**Recommended level:** Intermediate to advanced.


**[Find Lana Blakely on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Lana+Blakely+official+YouTube)**


If you enjoy thoughtful conversations about relationships, self-awareness, confidence, and life choices, Lana Blakely’s content may be a useful addition to your listening routine.


Personal essays and reflective videos expose you to language beyond the standard classroom topics of food, travel, and introductions.


You’ll encounter expressions for describing feelings, explaining experiences, comparing viewpoints, and discussing abstract ideas.


**Try this:** Write down an expression that helps you describe an emotion or opinion. Use it in a short spoken reflection about your own day.


You don’t need to agree with every idea in a video. Understanding a viewpoint and explaining your own response is excellent communication practice.


### **15. Matt D’Avella — Improve Your Habits While Practising English**


**Best for:** Productivity, minimalism, habits, focus, and self-improvement.


**Recommended level:** Intermediate to advanced, depending on the video.


**[Watch Matt D’Avella on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@mattdavella)**


Matt D’Avella creates content around habits, productivity, minimalism, and personal development. His videos can help you explore practical ideas while listening to longer explanations in English.


This is especially useful if you want to develop your ability to follow a narrative, understand opinions, and describe cause-and-effect relationships.


**Try this:** After watching a video about habits, explain one idea you want to apply in your life.


For example: “I’m going to practise English for 15 minutes every day instead of waiting until I have an entire free hour.”


You have now practiced English and created an actionable habit. Two wins, one video.


## Best YouTube Channels for Advanced English and Intellectual Growth


If you already understand everyday English, the next challenge is learning to discuss complicated subjects, follow unfamiliar accents, and express nuanced opinions.


These channels offer content that can stretch your vocabulary and listening skills while encouraging critical thinking.


### **Vox — Learn English Through News, Culture and Explainers**


**Best for:** Current affairs, social issues, history, culture, and advanced vocabulary.


**Recommended level:** Upper-intermediate to advanced.


**[Watch Vox on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Vox)**


Vox explains complex topics through visual storytelling, research-based explainers, and documentary-style videos.


Its content is useful for learners who want to understand discussions about society, technology, politics, culture, and global events.


However, some videos contain dense vocabulary and fast narration, so don’t be discouraged if you need to replay sections.


**Try this:** Choose a topic you already understand in your first language. Watch a short explainer, identify five unfamiliar expressions, and summarise the main argument aloud.


This helps you practise explaining complex ideas rather than simply repeating memorised sentences.


### **Jared Henderson — Practise English Through Philosophy**


**Best for:** Critical thinking, philosophy, meaning, and abstract discussions.


**Recommended level:** Upper-intermediate to advanced.


**[Find Jared Henderson on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Jared+Henderson+official+YouTube)**


Philosophical discussions challenge you to follow arguments, consider different perspectives, and explain abstract concepts.


Jared Henderson’s content can be useful for learners who want to explore such ideas while developing the language needed to express nuanced thoughts.


Instead of only learning practical phrases such as “Could you help me?”, you’ll also encounter language used to discuss purpose, identity, society, and personal beliefs.


**Try this:** After watching, answer three questions in English:


- What was the main argument?


- Do I agree or disagree, and why?


- What example supports my opinion?


This is especially useful for advanced conversation practice, academic discussions, and **[interviews](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/practice-for-a-job-interview-english-speaking-skills-that-get-you-hired/)** that require more than short answers.


### **Dr. Easy Celely — Explore Psychology and Self-Improvement**


**Best for:** Psychology-related topics, learning strategies, self-confidence, and reflective listening.


**Recommended level:** Intermediate to advanced, depending on the subject.


**[Find Dr. Easy Celely on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Dr+Easy+Celely+official+YouTube)**


If you enjoy understanding how people think, learn, and develop confidence, this channel is worth exploring.


Its described focus on psychology, learning, and self-improvement can help you encounter **[vocabulary](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog/7-best-vocabulary-building-apps-for-students-in-2026/)**


used to discuss behaviour, motivation, and personal development.


Choose videos that match your interests and language level. More specialised topics may introduce terminology that requires additional explanation.


**Try this:** Learn three useful words from a video and use them to explain a concept in simple English.


The goal isn’t to sound like a psychology textbook. It’s to explain an idea clearly enough that another person understands it.


## MySivi: Turn English Lessons into Speaking Practice


Let’s address the problem that many English learners face.


You can understand a video, remember a useful phrase, and even pronounce it correctly when repeating after the teacher. But when a colleague asks you a question unexpectedly, your brain suddenly opens 37 tabs, and none of them responds.


This is the gap between


**knowing English and using English** .


**[YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FO5-Ywn818)**


is excellent for learning through listening, demonstrations, explanations, and examples. However, watching a video alone doesn’t automatically give you the experience of responding to another person in a live conversation.


That’s where **[MySivi](https://www.mysivi.ai/)**


can complement your learning routine.


**[Watch MySivi’s English-learning video: Fluent English in 15 Days!](https://youtu.be/XBuZYSn0Lqk?si=T0QI12VsHqGjSnsX)**


MySivi is an English-speaking practice app featuring an AI tutor, designed to help learners practise conversations and develop their communication skills. Depending on the features available to your account, you can explore conversational scenarios and work on areas such as pronunciation, grammar, and sentence structure.


Here’s how to combine it with your favourite **[YouTube channels](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FO5-Ywn818)**


.


### **The Watch–Shadow–Speak Method**


**Step 1: Watch and learn**


Choose a five-to-ten-minute lesson from BBC Learning English, English with Lucy, or another channel you enjoy.


Write down three useful expressions.


For example:


- “Let me think about that.”


- “From my point of view…”


- “Could you explain that again?”


**Step 2: Shadow the speaker**


Replay a short section and speak along with the speaker. Pay attention to pronunciation, pauses, word stress, and intonation.


Repeat the section until you can say it more comfortably.


**Step 3: Speak using what you learned**


Open **[MySivi](https://www.mysivi.ai/)**


and practice a relevant conversation where the appropriate feature is available.


If you learned expressions for sharing opinions, try using them in a discussion. If you learned interview vocabulary, practise answering interview-style questions.


Don’t simply repeat a memorised sentence. Respond to the question in your own words.


**Step 4: Review and improve**


Notice which expressions you used confidently and which ones were difficult to recall. Review the relevant lesson and practise again.


This approach gives you a practical way to connect listening, pronunciation, vocabulary, and speaking.


The aim isn’t to finish as many lessons as possible. It’s to make the language you learn easier to use when you need it.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid When Learning English on YouTube


Even the best English-learning channels won’t help much if your study habits prevent you from practising.


### **Mistake 1: Watching without speaking**


Listening helps you understand English, but speaking requires you to produce language yourself.


**Fix:** Pause after useful sentences and repeat them aloud. Then create your own examples.


### **Mistake 2: Switching between too many channels**


Following 25 teachers at once can leave you overwhelmed by different teaching styles, accents, and advice.


**Fix:** Choose two or three channels based on your current goals. Add more only when you have a clear reason.


### **Mistake 3: Memorising words without context**


Knowing a word’s meaning doesn’t guarantee you’ll use it naturally.


**Fix:** Learn complete phrases and create sentences connected to your life.


### **Mistake 4: Depending entirely on subtitles**


Subtitles can help, especially for beginners, but reading every word may keep you from training your listening skills.


**Fix:** Watch once without subtitles if the video is manageable. Then use English subtitles to check what you missed.


### **Mistake 5: Trying to eliminate your accent**


A strong accent isn’t automatically a communication problem. Unclear sounds, misplaced stress, or difficulty being understood may be more important to address.


**Fix:** Focus on intelligibility, pronunciation, rhythm, and confidence rather than trying to sound exactly like someone else.


### **Mistake 6: Expecting instant fluency**


A title promising fluency in a few days may be appealing, but sustainable progress depends on your starting level, practice, consistency, and opportunities to use English.


**Fix:** Set small goals. Learn three expressions, use them in conversation, and gradually increase the difficulty.


Remember: you don’t need perfect English to begin speaking. Speaking is one of the ways you improve.


## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)


**


**


Which YouTube channel is best for learning English in 2026?


The best channel depends on your goal. Rachel’s English is useful for American pronunciation, English with Lucy for British English and vocabulary, BBC Learning English for structured listening practice, and the **[MySivi](https://www.mysivi.ai/blog)**


YouTube channel for everyday conversations. Choose according to your level and learning needs rather than subscriber count alone.


**


**


Can I learn to speak English fluently by watching YouTube?


YouTube can help you improve listening, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. However, watching alone doesn’t guarantee speaking fluency. Combine videos with shadowing, self-recording, speaking exercises, and conversations so you learn to retrieve and use expressions without relying on subtitles.


**


**


Are there free YouTube channels to learn English?


Yes. The channels listed in this guide offer YouTube content you can explore without paying for a separate course, although individual creators may also offer paid courses or other services. You can start with BBC Learning English, Rachel’s English, English with Lucy, Learnex, and other channels that match your goals.


**


**


Which YouTube channels are useful for learning advanced English?


Vox and Jared Henderson can provide challenging listening material covering social issues, culture, philosophy, and abstract ideas. Choose topics you’re interested in, write down unfamiliar expressions, and summarise the main argument in your own words. Advanced practice should challenge you without making every video impossible to understand.


**


**


Can I improve my English while watching lifestyle and productivity videos?
